Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 22.1.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No. KA-40-W-4575 as a pillion rider, rode by one M.V.Chowdhari slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations from Besthrahalli to Y.N. Hosakote road, Y.N. Hosakote, Tumkur, when he reached near Sri Radhaswami Ashrama, at that time, driver of the car bearing registration No.AP-02-BR-2256 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Y.N. Hosakote Hospital, wherein he took the first aid treatment, then he was shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengalruru wherein he was treated as an inpatient and had spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 32 years, working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-02-BRE-2256.

In this regard,
case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Y.N. Hosakote Police in Crime No.9/2022 under section 279 and 337 of IPC & Section 187 of M.V. Act.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insured and the respondent No.3 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.

sentences.text: After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 have not appeared before the court, remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.3 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.3, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of car bearing No.AP-02-BR-2256 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-40-W- 4575 and not on the part of the driver of the car.
Further contended that the driver of the car had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
*ISSUES*
1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 22.1.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. Bestharahalli to Y.N. Hosakote road, near Shri Radhaswami Ashrama, Y.N. Hosakote, Tumkur, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HN-4171, in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?
9.
In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, petitioner has placed his affidavit evidence, in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Technician as PW2 and got marked at Ex.P18 to Ex.P21.

In addition this, placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P22 & Ex.P23.
10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.3 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner.

At the same time, the respondent No.1 & 2 being owner &
insured of the offending vehicle placed exparte.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

3 12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.AP-02-BR- 2256, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
14. On the other hand, the respondent No.3 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the manner of accident.
But not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.

The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner &
insured of the offending vehicle placed exparte.
In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the court to assess the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion in connection with the above fact in issue.
15. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P7
. Ex. P1-
true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.9/2022 of Y.N.Hosakote Police Station.
Ex. P2
-true copy of the first information statement given one Ranganatha.
Ex . P3
-true copy of the mahazar.
Ex.P4-true copy of the spot sketch.
Ex.P5-true copy of the IMV report, Ex.P6 -wound certificate of the petitioner.
Ex.P7- true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.9/2022 of Y.N.Hosakote Police.

16. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Ranganatha, the S.H.O. of Y.N.Hosakote Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 & 338 of I.P.C & Section 187 of IMV Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC & Section 187 of IMV Act.
17. The respondent No.3 ought to have been examined the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witness who witnessed the alleged accident to disprove the case of the petitioner.

For the reasons best known to the respondent No.3 neither examined the driver of the offending vehicle nor any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

18. Though the PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

From the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ravi Kumar vs Kodipalli Sreenivasulu on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152359232/
4 Ex.P9, it is no doubt that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.AP-02-BR-2256.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
19.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

20. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
Crush injury over right knee 22.
In connection with the above said injury, the doctor is of the opinion that the aforesaid injury is simple in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P8.
On going through the discharge summary of Kanva Sri Sai Hopital, Bengaluru reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 23.1.2022 to 2.2.2022.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of medical record technician of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital as PW2.

He has placed Authorisation letter, police intimation,
MLC extract and inpatient record as per Ex.P18 to Ex.P21.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW3.
PW3 has placed clinical note & x-ray as per Ex.P22 & Ex.P23.

Ravi Kumar vs Kodipalli Sreenivasulu on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152359232/
5

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injury and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
23.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a driver and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has placed salary certificate issued by SLV Toors & Travels, Y.N.Hosakote as per Ex.P9, which reveals that the petitioner was getting salaryt of Rs.700/- per day.
To prove the same, the petitioner has not examined his employer or his pass book to show the definite income.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken.
On going through the discharge summary of Kanva Sri Sai Hopital, Bengaluru reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 23.1.2022 to 2.2.2022.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one month by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,500/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
24.

The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.4,82,352/- as per Ex.P13 along with advance receipts and prescriptions as per Ex.P14 & Ex.P16.

At the time of cross-examination except the suggestion that the medical bills are created, nothing has been placed on record to to prove that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,82,352/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
25.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
The petitioner has produced one ambulance bill marked at Ex.P15 for Rs.850/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
26.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.

As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained simple injury, but he took Ravi Kumar vs Kodipalli Sreenivasulu on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152359232/
6 the treatment for degloving injury for a period of 7 days.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summary for consideration.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N. examined as PW3.
PW3 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained right knee degloving injury.
For which the petitioner was treated with wound debridement with LD flap and SSG on 26.1.2022 and later he was discharged with regular follow-up treatment
. PW2 being the Medical Record Technician has placed Police intimation, MLC extract and inpatient record as per Ex.P19 to Ex.P21.
He has been cross-examined by the respondent No.2.
But nothing has been elicited from his mouth.

27. PW3 has stated that, at the time of his examination the petitioner has swollen right knee with an unhealthy scar over the right knee and evidence of flap and SSG, x-ray shows the right knee staples in the soft tissue around the knee joint.
The petitioner has placed laboratory report and x-rays as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P17.
On the basis of entire evaluation of the disability of the petitioner, PW3 had opined that, total physical disability of right lower limb is 40% and that of his whole body at 13%.

In support of his evidence produced clinical note and x- ray as per Ex.P22 & Ex.P23.
28.
At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that he is not treated doctor.
The petitioner undergone plastic surgery.
PW2 denied the suggestion that due to the plastic surgery the petitioner had no scar marks and there is no loss of muscles.
Based on the documents he has assessed the physical disability.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
29. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW3 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW3 seems little bit exorbitant.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 10% instead of 13%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
30. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 32 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card and driving licence marked at Ex.P10 & Ex.P11 for consideration.
On going through the said documents, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 4.6.1990 & 30.5.1990.
The accident occurred on 22.1.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 32 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '16' is to be taken into consideration.

31. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, he was working as a driver and getting an income of Rs.40,000/- per month.
As already discussed above, though the petitioner has placed salary certificate, but not examined his employer, acquaintance book or bank pass book to prove the said income.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.

sentences.text:
In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injury sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X 12 X 16 X10/100= Rs.2,97,600/-.
Loss of amenities;
33.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he cannot walk for long distance, he cannot sit, squat, movements of right knee, cannot use Indian toilet, and there are scar marks present over the body and undergoing deep mental shock.

On perusal of evidence of PW3 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
34. In connection with the future medication, PW3 has not stated about the future medication.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled to award compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

35. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 30,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 15,500-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.4,82,352-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.2,97,600-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.
Future medication Nil Total Rs.8,54,852-00 36.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,54,852/- (Rupees eight lakh fifty four thousand eight hundred and fifty two only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text:
As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.AP-02-BR-2256,
alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insured and the respondent No.3 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
38.
As per the records insurance policy was valid from 28.8.2021 to 27.8.2022.
The alleged accident had taken place on 22.1.2022.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insured and the respondent No.3 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
39.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.8,54,852/- (Rupees  eight lakh fifty four thousand eight  hundred and fifty two only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

For the reasons best known to the respondent No.3 neither examined the driver of the offending vehicle nor any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
18. Though the PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
By taking into consideration of the nature of the injury and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insured and the respondent No.3 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
38.
As per the records insurance policy was valid from 28.8.2021 to 27.8.2022.
The alleged accident had taken place on 22.1.2022.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insured and the respondent No.3 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
